item.description: LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. Kids will explore: • Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components • Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect) • Testing, debugging, and iterating designs • Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas Details: • 60-minute session • Small-group format • No prior experience required Community Spons

Finding Sensitive Data Before Masking: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline — Thu Aug 27, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Cloud Data Driven **Presentation Title:** Finding Sensitive Data Before Masking: A Human-in-the-Loop Pipeline for Enterprise Test Data
**Abstract:** Most data masking projects begin with a list of columns to transform. But where did that list come from? And what happens when sensitive information is hidden in fields such as notes, comments, and free-text descriptions?
This session presents a practical, human-in-the-loop pipeline for identifying sensitive columns before production data is copied into test environments. The workflow combines column-name and pattern signals, historical masking decisions, sampled values, NLP and LLM review, and final analyst approval.
Using an enterprise Test Data Management case study, I will explain how this approach reduced sensitive-data analysis time for a medium-sized schema of approximately 100 tables from about 64 hours to about 2 hours, while reaching approximately 93% agreement with parallel manual review. item.title: Understanding Medicare — Wed Sep 16, 11:00 AM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Confused about Medicare? Join us for an informative session that breaks down the basics of this federal health insurance program. Learn who qualifies, including adults age 65 and older, younger individuals with disabilities, and those with End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD).
We’ll explain the different parts of Medicare—Part A (hospital insurance), Part B (medical insurance), and Part D (prescription drug coverage)—and what services each covers. The program will also explore your coverage options, including Original Medicare with supplemental (Medigap) plans and Medicare Advantage (Part C).
This session is ideal for anyone approaching Medicare eligibility, caregivers, or those looking to better understand their health coverage choices.
Presented by Medicare Specialist Jacki Spear.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

Bring your knitting, crocheting, needlepoint, embroidery, cross-stitch, quilting, or other portable craft and enjoy conversation with fellow readers and makers.
There is no assigned book—everyone is welcome to share what they're reading, discover new titles, and connect with others in the community while creating something by hand.
Bring a project you're working on, or start something new! Thanks to generous donations from our community, we'll often have a small selection of craft supplies available to share, though materials will vary from meeting to meeting. If you have a specific project in mind, we encourage you to bring your own supplies.
